qe/eion.head: θέειον
qe/eion.i: -ου, τό. Also θήϊον Od. 22.493. Sulphur.

rows.z: In reference to the sulphurous smell associated with a thunderbolt

qeo/s.head: θεός
qeo/s.i: -οῦ, ὁ, ἡ. Instrumental θεόφιν. With a word expressing likeness Il. 7.366, Il. 14.318, Il. 17.477: Od. 3.110, 409. This form as ablative Il. 17.101, Il. 23.347.

rows.z: A god as distinguished in terms from a goddess
Without reference to any particular god, the divine power, heaven

ex.g: θεός που σοὶ τό γʼ ἔδωκεν

rows.z: A goddess as distinguished in terms from a woman
In pl., the gods: τίς θεῶν;
In pl., the gods as distinguished in terms from the goddesses

ex.g: πάντες τε θεοὶ πᾶσαί τε θέαιναι
πρός τε θεῶν πρός τʼ ἀνθρώπων

qe/aina.head: θέαινα
qe/aina.i: ἡ [fem. as θεά. Cf. λέαινα, lioness.]

rows.z: A goddess as distinguished from a god

ex.g: πάντες τε θεοὶ πᾶσαί τε θέαιναι
χωσαμένη ὅ οἱ οὔ τι θ. ῥέξεν

rows.z: Eating the heart, that will not leave the heart in peace.
Like the gods, godlike. Epithet of persons
(πολύαρνι). Son of Pelops, brother of Atreus and father of Aegisthus. The sceptre left to him by Atreus and by him to Agamemnon
A rushing or violent wind or storm

ex.g: κονίη ἵσταθʼ ὥς τε νέφος ἠὲ θ.

qumarh/s.head: θυμαρής
qumarh/s.i: -ές [θυμός + ἀρ-, ἀραρίσκω. Fitted to the heart.] Neut. in form θυμῆρες Od. 10.362.

rows.z: Such as to inspire affection, lovely, beauteous
Suited to one's taste, grateful to the senses: [ὕδωρ] θυμῆρες κεράσασα (till it became. . .)
The hairs of the mane of a horse
The hairs of a horse's tail
The hair on the head of an ox
Of or pertaining to the sea

qespe/sios.head: θεσπέσιος
qespe/sios.i: -η, -ον [θε-, θεός + σ(ε)π-. See ἐννέπω.]

rows.z: Absol. in fem., sentence pronounced by a god, the will of heaven

ex.g: εἰ καὶ θεσπεσίῃ πόλιν οὐκ ἀλαπάξεις

rows.z: Of song, befitting a god, divinely sweet
Of singers, heavenly sweet of voice
a Of shouting or lamentation, such as might come from a god's throat, immense, deafening
Of inarticulate sounds. Of the sound of branches of trees smiting each other
The force of the second element lost a Of or pertaining to the gods, divine
Indicating a high degree of some quality such as abundance, greatness, greatness of extent, completeness, swiftness, beauty, sweetness or the like
To come often to, frequent, an indicated place

ex.g: πάρος γε μὲν οὔ τι θαμίζεις

rows.z: To go about, ply one's vocation
With pass. pple., to be accustomed to treatment of an indicated kind

ex.e: was not wont to be (so) cared for

rows.z: Neut. pf. pple, pass. τεθυωμένον. To impart fragrance to

ex.g: ἐλαίῳ, τό ῥά οἱ τεθυωμένον ἦεν
ex.e: which she had by her in (full) fragrance

quga/thr.head: θυγάτηρ
quga/thr.i: ἡ [cognate with Eng. daughter, German tochter.]

rows.z: The root or bed (of the eye)
Recompense for rearing due by a child to his parents
Divine of form, godlike. Epithet of persons
Out through a door, out of a room or house
Of passing the gates of dreams
Forth from a specified or indicated space or region: [ἰχθὺν] ἔρριψε θ. (out of the sea)

ex.g: διὰ δʼ ἀμπερὲς ἦλθε θ. ἰός
ex.e: through and out from the axe-heads
from the line of the ships

rows.z: 3 sing. aor. pass. θρῡλίχθη. To crush, bruise
Of a boar whetting his tusks
Partaking of the nature of the gods, divine, immortal
(app. from the dance being regarded as a matter of ritual).
Of divine origin, from a divine source, divine
(app. as god-built; see 446 and cf. Il. 7.452, Il. 8.519)
Applied to persons of divine descent
(he was descended from Zeus; see Il. 20.215-232)
Applied to kings as holding their office from Zeus
To heralds as under his special protection
To bards as singing by divine inspiration
Applied as a mere epithet of honour to Odysseus
Denoting a superlative degree of excellence or beauty

qou=ros.head: θοῦρος
qou=ros.i: and in fem. form θοῦρις, -ιδος, with acc. -ιν [θορ-, θρῴσκω.] Rushing, impetuous, eager for the fray. Epithet

rows.z: Of a shield, app. by transference of epithet from the bearer to the shield
Absol., a mortal man, a man
App. vertical (presumably metal) pegs at the top and bottom of a side of a gate working in stone sockets and governing the opening and shutting

ex.g: Τρώων πόλις ἐπὶ πᾶσα βέβηκεν θ.

rows.z: (ἑπτάπυλος, εὐρύχορος , ἐϋστέφανος, ἱερὰ τείχεα , πολυήρατος). The Boeotian city, traditionally said to have been founded by Cadmus (represented as having been founded by Amphion-2 and Zethus Od. 11.262)

qrasumh/dhs.head: Θρασυμήδης
qrasumh/dhs.i: (ἀντίθεος, δῖος, ἱππόδαμος, κυδάλιμος, μενεπτόλεμος, ποιμὴν λαῶν , ὑπέρθυμος).

rows.z: To be of good heart or courage, of good cheer
In aor., to take heart, pluck up courage

ex.e: this is a great wonder that I see

rows.z: A town of uncertain site in the realm of Philoctetes
To run or flow (with a liquid)
To offer in sacrifice portions of a meal before partaking
To offer (such portions to the gods)
(app. a room built in the αὐλή and opening into the αἴθουσα near the πρόδομος; or perh. a portion of the αἴθουσα next the πρόδομος walled off). Cf.
(αὐλῆς app. local genit., in the . . . ; cf. Il. 9.473 above), ἐς θάλαμον ᾧ ἔνι κούρη κοιμᾶτο

ex.g: γήμας ἐκ θαλάμοιο μετὰ κλέος ἵκετʼ Ἀχαιῶν

rows.z: The sleeping-chamber occupied by a married pair
Of such a room in the palace of Zeus
A chamber appropriated to the lady of a house and her maidens
(the same as the μέγαρον of 125). Cf.
In pl. of the women's apartments generally

(cf. Od. 22.143 cited under (4); or this may be the pl. of indefiniteness like νύμφας in this line and γάμοι and εἰλαπίναι in the prec. line) (u.l. ἐς θαλάμους, which would go under 1.b): μυχῷ θαλάμων ἥμεθα
A room for storage or safe custody, a store-room, a treasure-chamber
(app. meaning a single room; cf. Il. 18.492 cited under (3)). Cf.

qauma/zw.head: θαυμάζω
qauma/zw.i: [θαῦμα.] 3 pl. pa. iterative θαυμάζεσκον Od. 19.229. 3 sing. fut. in mid. form θαυμάσσεται Il. 18.467. (ἀπο-.)

rows.z: To wonder, marvel, to feel or be struck with wonder, astonishment or admiration
To wonder or marvel at, look upon with wonder or eager curiousity
To look upon or behold (a person) with respectful wonder and admiration
Of bold spirit, stout of heart
App., mystic implements borne in the rites of Dionysus
To serve as a hired labourer
To teem with, abound in. With genit.

qe/sfatos.head: θέσφατος
qe/sfatos.i: -ον [the second element φα-, φημί. The first explained as θεσ-, θεός.]

rows.z: Pronounced or ordained by a god or by the divine will. Neut. in impers. construction
Absol. in neut. pl. θέσφατα, divine ordinances or decrees

ex.g: οὔ τι θεῶν ἐκ θ. ᾔδη

rows.z: Fragrant with the savour of sacrifice

qa/llw.head: †θάλλω
qa/llw.i: Pf. pple. τεθηλώς Od. 12.103.

rows.z: Of vegetation, to grow profusely, flourish, be luxuriant
In pf. pple. a Growing profusely, flourishing, luxuriant
Of autumn (the season of mellow fruitfulness)
Of the fat or lard of swine, rich
Of a feast, sumptuous, affording good cheer
(ἐπι-.) To encourage, hearten, cheer, put spirit into
Specifically, a fine in place of personal service in war
Patronymic Ἀνδραιμονίδης. Son of Andraemon and leader of the Aetolians
accepts Hector's challenge but does not get the lot
Thoas advises the chiefs to stand up to Hector, sending the general body back
in Odysseus's tale to Eumaeus and his companions
Of youths, lusty, in prime of vigour

ex.g: οὔ θήν μιν ἀνήσει θυμὸς νεικείειν
οὐ μέν θην κείνης γε χερείων εὔχομαι εἶναι

rows.z: A kind or mode of death

ex.e: one would feel more confidence, have better heart

qnh/|skw.head: θνῄσκω
qnh/|skw.i: Fut. infin. in mid. form θανέεσθαι Il. 4.12, Il. 15.728: Od. 20.21.

rows.z: In a quasi- passive sense of being slain in battle
In aor. indic. a In strict aor. sense

ex.g: οὔ κε θανόντι περ ὧδʼ ἀκαχοίμην

ex.e: let not thy death grieve thee

rows.z: Absol. in pl. pple., the dead
In pf. a To be dead
coming, flying, falling, thick and fast
Occurring at short intervals over a space, numerous
Patronymic Ἡρακλεΐδης. Son of Heracles and father of Pheidippus and Antiphus-1

ex.e: the two words hardly to be distinguished

rows.z: To wonder, be struck with wonder or astonishment

qh=lus.head: θῆλυς
qh=lus.i: [θη-, θάομαι2.] Also in regular fem. form θήλεια Il. 2.767, Il. 8.7, Il. 11.681, Il. 20.222: Od. 4.636, Od. 9.439, Od. 14.16, Od. 21.23.

rows.z: Comp. θηλυτέρη, female as opposed to male
A tassel or pendant. Attached to the aegis
(app. of twisted wire). To Here's girdle
Wife of Peleus and mother of Achilles. Comes when called upon by Achilles on his loss of Briseis
Achilles reminds her how she saved Zeus from bonds
she promises to induce Zeus to favour the Trojans
goes to him and gets his promise
received Dionysus when terrified by Lycourgus-1
the chest given by her to Achilles
comes to Achilles on the death of Patroclus
sent to bid Achilles release Hector's corpse
appears and takes part in the funeral rites of Achilles
the jar given by her to receive Achilles's bones
the prizes given by her for his funeral games
Quick in movement, nimble, swift, fleet
Of night (app. thought of as a body of darkness passing swiftly over the earth)
Of a whip, quickly making itself felt
Of a meal, perh., deftly served
Doubtfully explained (cf. θοόω) as the sharp or pointed islands, supposed to form part of the group called the Echinades.

qeopro/pos.head: θεοπρόπος
qeopro/pos.i: [app., one who prays to a god, fr. θεός + προπ-, perh. conn. with L. precor.]

rows.z: One who reveals the divine will, a seer
(cf. Il. 21.526 cited under θεῖος 4).
A warrior in honourable personal attendance on another, the relation of the two resembling generally that of squire and knight
A young shoot or branch. Fig. of a youthful person

ex.g: οὐκ ἔχει θράσος ὅς κεν ἴδηται

rows.z: Patronymic Αἰγεΐδης. Son of Aegeus, king of Athens, and husband of Phaedra. The great legendary hero of Athens. Named as a warrior of Nestor's youth

ex.e: much matter that was to be his death-warrant

qu/rh.head: θύρη
qu/rh.i: -ης, ἡ. Locative θύρηφι(ν) Od. 9.238, Od. 22.220.

rows.z: a The door of a room
In pl. (properly of a double or folding door; cf. Od. 17.267), the door of a house or room

ex.g: προπάροιθε θυράων (i.e. the main door of the μέγαρον)

rows.z: Of the entrance to the cave of the Cyclops
Of the entrances to the cave of the Naiads
Of the door of a pigsty
a The gate of the αὐλή

ex.g: αὐλὴν ποίησαν θύρην δʼ ἔχε μοῦνος ἐπιβλής

rows.z: (the same as the θύρην of 453): ἔκτοσθεν αὐλῆς ὄρχατος ἄγχι θυράων
In locative at the door. Hence, outside

ex.g: κτήματα, τά τʼ ἔνδοθι καὶ τὰ θύρηφιν

rows.z: In mid., to become warm or hot
Patronymic Κισσηΐς. Daughter of Cisses (Il. 11.224), wife of Antenor, mother of Iphidamas and priestess at Troy of Athene . Brought up Pedaeus
opens Athene's temple for the aged women

qa/sswn.head: θάσσων
qa/sswn.i: -ονος [for θακίων. Comp. of ταχύς with transference of aspirate.]

rows.z: In neut. θᾶσσον as adv. a The quicker, the speedier, the sooner
Quickly rather than slowly, quickly, with speed

qoo/w.head: θοόω
qoo/w.i: [poss. conn. with θοός and meaning orig. to make quick or active, acquiring the sense of sharpening when applied to weapons, etc..]

rows.z: To sharpen, put a point upon: ἐθόωσα [ῥόπαλον.] i 327.
Trojan. Son of Phaenops-1. With his brother Xanthus-3 killed by Diomedes

qespidah/s.head: θεσπιδαής
qespidah/s.i: -ές (θεσπιδαϝής) [θε-σπ- as in θεσπέσιον (with the force of the second element lost) + δα(ϝ)-, δαίω1.]

rows.z: Epithet of fire, defying human efforts, devouring, consuming
As distinguished from ὀπώρη, early summer

qhri/on.head: θηρίον
qhri/on.i: τό [prob. θήρ + suffix distinguishing an individual from a class.]

qe/w.head: θέω
qe/w.i: [θεϝ-.] Also θείω [prob. for θή(ϝ)ω, fr. θηϝ-, long form of θεϝ-.] 3 pl. pa. iterative θέεσκον Il. 20.229. 2 sing. fut. in mid. form θεύσεαι Il. 23.623.

rows.z: Of men, horses, etc., to run, speed
To run a race, contend in a race
Of the motion of a ship
Of a person in a ship

ex.g: ὅτε κεῖνος ἐν νηυσὶ Μαλειάων ὄρος ἷξε θέων

rows.z: Of things, to run or extend
Trojan. Son of Enops-1. Killed by Patroclus
A means of enchantment, a spell
A means of propitiating or placating
Distinguished in terms from the land
From the land and the heavens

(ἱερή, ὑποπλακίη, ὑψίπυλος). A town (inhabited by the Cilices), of which Eetion-1 was king, in the plain of Thebe-2 in which Adramyttium afterwards stood. Taken by Achilles and Eetion-1 slain and Chryseis captured
In pl., a body of traditionary rules or precedents

ex.g: βασιλεύς, ᾧ δῶκε κρόνου πάϊς θέμιστας

rows.z: (has no regard for any usage of decency; see εἴδω III.12).
What is established or sanctioned by custom or usage

ex.g: ἣ θ. ἐστὶν ἤ τʼ ἀνδρῶν ἤ τε γυναικῶν
ξείνια παρέθηκεν, ἅ τε ξείνοις θ. ἐστίν
ex.e: which by the customs of hospitality one . . .

ex.g: ἄορ ἔχων: τῷ δʼ οὐ θ. ἐστὶ μιγῆναι

rows.z: (as it is his privilege to do)

ex.e: as a woman's way ever is
since it is my right to . . .
for that is due to him who . . .

rows.z: An oracular reply (in answer to an inquiry as to what is right to be done)
As proper name, a goddess with such funtions as may be gathered from the name and the context
See θέμις 7 in Lexicon.
Supports, consisting of stakes or stones, set to contain the face of an earthwork or mound (cf. στήλη 1)
Prob. a plank or gangway connecting the forward and after ἴκρια of a ship

ex.g: ἀνεχάζετο θρῆνυν ἐφʼ ἑπταπόδην, λίπε δʼ ἴκρια

rows.z: A beast of prey, perh. the jackal
Only in phrase ἐπὶ θρωσμῷ πεδίοιο, a piece of ground rising from, and somewhat above the general level of, the plain
To cleanse with the fumes of sulphur
(ἀνα-, ἀπο-, ἐκ-, ἐν-, ἐπι-, ἐσ-, προ-, ὑπερ-.) To leap, spring, bound, dart
Epithet of war, carried on with spirit, strenous
App., the palm of the hand

qe/lgw.head: θέλγω
qe/lgw.i: 3 sing. pa. iterative θέλγεσκε Od. 3.264. 3 fut. θέλξει Od. 16.298.

rows.z: To work upon by spells or enchantment, bewithch, charm
Sim. of the operation of passion
Of divine interference, to lay a spell upon, bind up from activity
To work upon by wiles, cajole, lead on to one's hurt, prejudice, or dishonour
To beguile, deceive, cheat: δόλῳ [μιν] ἔθελγεν

ex.g: οἶα μυθεῖται, θέλγοιτό κέ τοι ἦτορ

quosko/os.head: θυοσκόος
quosko/os.i: -ου, ὁ [θυ-, θύος + σκο- as in σκοπός.]

rows.z: App. a religious adviser skilled in divination from sacrifices, perh. from observation of the smoke thereof
A female divine (or semi-divine) being, a goddess
A goddess as distinguished in terms from a god
With the name of a particular goddess.
A Thracian bard deprived by the Muses at Dorium of his power of song
Trojan. A Paeonian. Killed by Achilles
Of a woman, blooming, in pride of beauty
Of marriage, app. giving the notion of the union of a pair in prime of youth
Of parts of the body, well-developed, stout
Of a horse's mane, long, flowing
A making of sacrifice, a sacrifice or offering
In pl. of a single offering
A tree not identified, the wood of which emits (sweet) odour when burnt
See Ἀκτορίων. Son of Eurytus-2 and grandson of Poseidon. A leader of the Epeians
(κατα-.) To pay funeral rites to (a corpse)
The beach or shore of the sea
The beach or shore (of the sea)
App., a piece of the shore covered by shallow water

ex.g: ὡς ὅτʼ ἀναπάλλεται ἰχθὺς θίνʼ ἐν φυκιόεντι

qumo/s.head: θυμός
qumo/s.i: -οῦ, ὁ. The heart, breast, soul, mind (cf. ἦτορ, καρδίη, κραδίη, κῆρ, φρήν).

rows.z: As the seat or a seat (when coupled with φρήν, φρένες, κραδίη hardly to be distinguished therefrom)
Of life; hence a Vitality, the vital powers, strength (cf. ἦτορ 2.a.α, κῆρ 2.a)

ex.g: εἰς ὅ κεν αὖτις θυμὸν λάβητε

rows.z: The animating principle, the vital spirit, the soul, the life, life, one's life (cf. αἰών 3, ἦτορ 2.a.β, μένος 7, ψυχή 1): τάχʼ ἂν θυμὸν ὀλέσσῃ
The spirit or soul thought of as distinct from the body and as leaving it at death (cf. ψυχή 4): θ. ᾤχετʼ ἀπὸ μελέων
Of spirit, courage, stoutness, resolution, endurance

ex.g: ὅν τινα θ. ἐμοὶ μαχέσασθαι ἀνώγει

rows.z: In reference to animals or insects

ex.g: σοὶ ἄλληκτον θυμὸν ἐνὶ στήθεσσι θεοὶ θέσαν
ὑμέτερος θ. καὶ ἀεικέα ἔργα φαίνεται

rows.z: Of madness, rage, fury, wild excitement
(of dogs) (see Il. 21.65, etc., under 4.a). Cf.
(περί advbl., exceedingly in his heart; cf. Il. 22.70 under 3.b and Od. 14.146 under (6)), αἲ γάρ με μένος καὶ θ. ἀνείη . . . (desire for vengeance)
(of a hawk). One's wishes or liking

ex.g: οὐδὲ λύκοι τε καὶ ἄρνες ὁμόφρονα θυμὸν ἔχουσιν

rows.z: Of feelings, emotions, moods, such as joy, grief, affection, dislike, pity, hope, fear, resentment, reverence, regard, solicitude, wonder, etc.
(see Il. 21.65, etc., under 4.a),
(dogs). One's good will or favour (cf. ἀποθύμιος): ἀπὸ θυμοῦ μᾶλλον ἐμοὶ ἔσεαι
Of the faculty of perception or knowledge: ᾔδεε κατὰ θυμὸν ὡς . . .
Of the faculty of thinking, deliberating, judging, considering, devising, conjecturing

ex.g: ταῦθʼ ὥρμαινε κατὰ φρένα καὶ κατὰ θυμόν
ἥδε οἱ κατὰ θυμὸν ἀρίστη φαίνετο βουλή

ex.e: as if a second inward voice admonished him

rows.z: (app., you did well in not hitting . . .),

ex.g: ὥς τοι θ. ἤπια δήνεα οἶδεν

ex.e: what manner of man I am

rows.z: II Vaguely as the seat of

ex.g: κῆρ 2.g: ἐμὸν κῆρ ἄχνυται ἐν θυμῷ

rows.z: III One's inward self as a region in which something takes place without outward manifestation

ex.e: without letting any outward sign appear

rows.z: IV In a more or less physical sense
Paining or burdening the heart, painful, distressing, grievous

qe/skelos.head: θέσκελος
qe/skelos.i: [the first element seems to be the same as in θέσ-φατος.]

rows.z: App., marvellous, wondrous, or the like
So in neut. θέσκελον as adv., marvellously, in wondrous wise

ex.g: αὐλῆς θ. (app., a door leading to the αὐλή from the λαύρη)

rows.z: In act., to cause to arm for the fray, get under arms
In mid. and pass. a to arm oneself for the fray, get under arms, don one's harness

ex.g: δός μοι τὰ σὰ τεύχεα θωρηχθῆναι

rows.z: App. meaning little more than to have one's station, post oneself, stand, be
of no great size, within the αὐλή, of unknown nature and use

ex.g: θητός, ὁ. A labourer for hire

qw=kos.head: θῶκος
qw=kos.i: -ου, ὁ Also θόωκος Od. 2.26, Od. 12.318 [θο-, θα-, θαάσσω.]

ex.g: οὔθʼ ἡμετέρη ἀγορὴ γένετʼ οὔτε θόωκος

rows.z: (the two words hardly to be distinguished). Cf.
To warm, to make flexible by the application of heat
Son of Polypheides and great-grandson of Melampus. In flight from Argos-1 (1) encounters Telemachus embarking for home at Pylus
is committed to the care of Peiraeus
To finish off the upper part of the wall of (an enclosure) with something intended to give protection or to prevent exit: ἐθρίγκωσεν [αὐλὴν] ἀχέρδῳ
3 sing. fut. mid. θλίψεται. To press or rub
Pres. pple. θαλπιόων. To be warm
To drive or carry in a specified direction
Endeavouring to rally one's spirit, making a fight for life
Nom. pl. masc. fut. pple. θαυμανέοντες. To witness or watch with eager interest
Biting the heart, stinging to action
(Cf. δάκε φρένας μῦθος Il. 5.493.)
3 pl. aor. opt. θησαίατο. To admire, look at with admiration

qa/omai.head: †θάομαι2
qa/omai.i: [θη- as τι-θή-νη.] Non-thematic pres. infin. θῆσθαι Od. 4.89.

ex.e: double acc. of whole and part, a woman's breast

rows.z: From, at the hands of, the gods: θ. οὐκ ἔστʼ ἀλέασθαι [θάνατον]
A nymph, daughter of Phorcys-2 and by Poseidon mother of Polyphemus-1
Epithet or the name of the island containing the oxen of the Sun
To do service to, serve. With dat.
Pleasing to the heart, desirable, choice
A female servant in charge of the sleeping-rooms, a chamber-maid

qeilo/pedon.head: θειλόπεδον
qeilo/pedon.i: τό [app. θείλη = εἵλη, the sun's warmth + πέδον, the ground.]

rows.z: A warm spot in a vineyard in which the grapes were left to be dried by the sun, a sun-trap
An uppermost course in a wall, a coping
A frieze running along the upper part of the inner walls of a house
To pronounce judgments, act as judge
With genit. (like ἀνάσσω 3.a), to rule over, be master of
Something (in the passages cited a huge stone) placed to block up a door
The inhabitants of Thesprotia, a part of Epeirus extending southeast from the Thyamis
